images.filename: Kalaupapa leper colony in 1905.jpg
images.caption: The Kalaupapa leper colony in 1905. There were approximately 750 living on the Kalaupapa peninsula at the time and included Stephen Mahelona Napela. Brother Dutton, in the center with the white beard, worked with Father Damien and also remained on Molokai until he died in 1931.

images.filename: Kalaupapa Village, Molokai Hawaii (15477918821).jpg
images.caption: Kalaupapa is on an isolated area of the island of Molokai.  This is the location of Hawaii's only leprosy colony first established as a prison in 1866, but now a refuge and national park.  There are no patients remaining with active leprosy, but some of the older Hawaii residents, now cured, still live there.  It is a beautiful village, but very difficult to reach - mainly by mule or hiking down some of the steepest cliffs in the world, or reaching it by small airplane.
